note: config_views (Configuration Entity View) exposes a Views base table per config-entity type named config_<prefix with . as _> (node.type -> config_node_type, user.role -> config_user_role, image.style -> config_image_style, system.menu -> config_system_menu, views.view -> config_views_view), backed by the views_config_entity_query query plugin (Entity Query API). It ships ~14 default Views (some enabled e.g. content_types at admin/structure/types, some disabled e.g. user_roles) and an EntityReferenceSelection plugin config_views. No settings form, permissions, or Drush. Medium/hard cases create/inspect namespaced cv_* Views on those config base tables via drush; verify checks the View's base_table.

evals.prompt: Using the config_views (Configuration Entity View) Drupal module, I want to build a View that lists user roles. What Views base table would that View use, and how is that base-table name derived from the config entity type?
evals.expected_output: config_user_role. config_views names each base table config_ + the config entity type's config prefix with dots replaced by underscores; user.role -> config_user_role (likewise node.type -> config_node_type, image.style -> config_image_style).

evals.prompt: How does config_views let Views query configuration entities that have no SQL content table? Name the Views query plugin it uses and what API that plugin runs.
evals.expected_output: It provides a Views query plugin views_config_entity_query (ConfigEntityQuery) that extends the SQL query plugin but executes the Entity Query API against config entity storage instead of SQL.

evals.prompt: Out of the box, config_views can replace some core admin listing pages with Views. Which shipped View takes over the Content types listing at admin/structure/types, and how do you opt into the ones that ship disabled (like User roles)?
evals.expected_output: The content_types View provides admin/structure/types. Some default Views ship disabled (e.g. user_roles, text_formats, view_modes, views_list); enable them at Structure > Views (or drush views:enable) to have them take over the corresponding admin list.

evals.prompt: This site has a View with machine id cv_known created with config_views. Inspect the live View configuration and state which Views base table it is built on (and therefore which kind of configuration entity it lists).
evals.expected_output: cv_known is built on the config_image_style base table, so it lists image style configuration entities. (drush cget views.view.cv_known base_table)

evals.prompt: A View with id cv_roles_known exists on this site (built with config_views). Inspect the live configuration and determine which configuration entity type it lists.
evals.expected_output: It lists user roles: views.view.cv_roles_known has base_table config_user_role.

evals.prompt: On this site, use config_views to create a View with machine id cv_roles that lists all User role configuration entities (base table config_user_role, query plugin views_config_entity_query). A single default display listing the roles is enough. Save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: views.view.cv_roles exists with base_table config_user_role (a config_views base table).

evals.prompt: Using config_views on this Drupal site, build a View named cv_styles that lists the site's image styles as configuration entities (it should use the config_views image-style base table). Save it to the live site.
